title: Personal Credit Cards: automatic payment instructions and their source account
content:
# Personal Credit Cards: automatic payment (autopay)

This policy covers the automatic payment instruction on a Personal Credit Cards account: what autopay debits and when, which account may fund it, who gives the instruction, and when a cancellation takes effect.

## Policy clauses

1. Automatic payment debits the named PCB checking account on the due date, for one of three amounts: the minimum due, the statement balance, or a fixed amount, but never more than the statement balance.
2. The autopay source account must be a checking account of the same customer in active status.
3. Setting up or changing autopay is the cardholder's own instruction.
4. Cancelling takes effect for due dates at least 3 calendar days after the change is recorded.

## Instruction options

| Option | What is debited on each due date |
|---|---|
| none | nothing |
| minimum due | the statement's minimum payment due |
| statement balance | the full statement balance |
| fixed amount | the fixed monthly amount, never more than the statement balance |

For every option other than a fixed amount, the fixed monthly amount on the instruction is 0.00.

## Source account check

The source account is checked in the bank's checking account records: it must belong to the same customer as the card and be in active status. A savings account, another person's account or a checking account that is not active does not meet this requirement.

## Cancellation timing (hypothetical dates)

A cancellation recorded on 10 June:
- takes effect for a due date of 13 June or later, which is at least 3 calendar days after the change;
- is not yet effective for a due date of 12 June, which is only 2 calendar days after the change, so that due date remains outside the cancellation.

## Basis Q&A

**Q: Can a fixed amount instruction debit more than the statement balance?**
A: No. The debit is never more than the statement balance.

**Q: Who sets up or changes autopay?**
A: The cardholder; setting up or changing autopay is the cardholder's own instruction.
